description:
> *This was generated by AI during research for docs/research/elixir-compilers-and-idioms.md.*

Kernel bodies match module aliases unexpanded (`{:__aliases__, _, [:Defk, :Bits]}` in compiler.ex and elixir_mode.ex). With `alias Defk.Bits`, `Bits.clz(x)` is rejected with `unsupported-call` ("Bits.clz/1 is not in the kernel subset"), while `Defk.Bits.clz(x)` compiles and returns 63 for 1. Reproduced 2026-10-12 in a scratch Mix app. A `def` would honour the alias, so this is a lexical-scope difference from ordinary Elixir.

Fix suggested by the docs (not tried): expand alias nodes with `Macro.expand/2` against `__CALLER__` at the `defk` call, which keeps compile tracers firing; `Macro.Env.expand_alias/4` is meant for tools, not macros. Decide whether `alias Enum, as: E` style aliases should be accepted too. See the note's alias-expansion section.
title: Aliased builtin calls in a kernel (alias Defk.Bits; Bits.clz(x)) are rejected as unsupported calls
